# `multilingual/` — optional, and honest about being optional

**Manifest ids:** `handbook-de-v1` (DOCX, German), `faq-es-v1` (DOCX, Spanish) · **Status:** AUTHORED — generated by `../../../tools/generate_corpus.py`

§21.2 lists multilingual questions as *"if supported"*. This directory and the three `m-*` cases
are therefore **conditional**: if the product does not claim multilingual support, drop the
category wholesale — delete `golden/cases/multilingual.yaml`, remove these two manifest entries,
and bump `VERSION`. Do **not** keep the cases and mark them expected-to-fail; a permanently red
row is a row everyone learns to skip past, including on the day it turns red for a new reason.

**Do not machine-translate these fixtures.** A fixture nobody on the team can read cannot be
graded during human review, and a mistranslation becomes an unexplained score. If no reviewer
reads German or Spanish, use a language a reviewer does read, or drop the category.

## Retrieval property exercised

Three distinct things, which is why there are three cases and not one:

1. **Same-language retrieval and answering** — a German question retrieves the German document
   and is answered in German (`m-001`).
2. **A second script-identical language** — Spanish, to confirm the first case did not pass
   because of English/German lexical overlap (`m-002`).
3. **Cross-lingual retrieval** — an **English** question whose only answer exists in the
   **German** document (`m-003`). This is the one that actually tests the embedding model's
   cross-lingual alignment; the other two can pass on lexical matching alone.

## Fixture 1 — `handbook-de-v1.docx`

A ~5-page **German localized edition** of the handbook — not a full translation, an extract:
Arbeitszeit (§2) and Urlaub (§3), stating the same numbers as `handbook-en-v1` (38-Stunden-Woche,
Kernzeit 10:00–16:00, 26 Urlaubstage, +1 Tag je 5 Dienstjahre, maximal 30).

Plus **one appendix that exists in no English document**:

> **Anhang DE — Betriebsrat**
> Der Betriebsrat tagt am **zweiten Dienstag jedes Monats**. Anträge sind spätestens eine Woche
> vorher einzureichen.

That appendix is the whole point of the fixture. A localized edition carrying a
country-specific section is realistic — this is not a translation artefact smuggled in to make a
case work. Case `m-003` asks, in English, when the works council meets; the only source is this
German appendix, and a correct answer is in **English**, citing `handbook-de-v1`.

## Fixture 2 — `faq-es-v1.docx`

A 2-page Spanish support FAQ restating, in Spanish, two facts that also exist in
`site-kelpwright-www`:

- *"El intervalo de calibración recomendado es de 12 meses. Los instrumentos en uso continuo en
  campo deben calibrarse cada 6 meses."*
- *"Las solicitudes de RMA deben presentarse en un plazo de 14 días desde la detección del fallo."*

Restating rather than introducing new facts is deliberate: `m-002` can then grade the **answer
language** independently of retrieval, because either source contains the fact and only one is in
Spanish. `expected_sources` for `m-002` lists both ids and `grading_notes` requires the answer to
be in Spanish.

## What the fixtures must NOT contain

- No fact that contradicts its English counterpart. The conflict fixture is `conflicting/`; an
  accidental second conflict across languages would be indistinguishable from a translation bug.
- No new facts in the Spanish FAQ beyond the two restatements.
- No English text in the German appendix — including the heading.

## Cases that depend on these fixtures

`m-001` `m-002` `m-003`.
